data.long_meaning: Ayeesah is the name of Asma bint Abu Bakr, one of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). She is also known as Umm al-Mumineen (Mother of the Believers). This name signifies respect, reverence, and love for the Prophet's wives, who played significant roles in the spread of Islam. The name Ayeesah carries the meaning “Mother of the believers” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ayeesah usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the believers and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Ayeeshah's father was a leading Meccan noble and an ardent opponent of Islam. Ayeeshah was married to the Prophet in Medina in 625 CE, shortly before the Battle of Uhud. Ayeeshah's family were enemies of Muhammad, but she converted to Islam in secret and later revealed her faith to her father, who was furious and tried to prevent her marriage to the Prophet. She was the daughter of Abu Bakr, the first caliph of Islam, and a close companion of the Prophet. Ayeeshah was married to the Prophet in Medina around 624 CE. She was known for her piety and scholarship, and her husband, Ali ibn Abi Talib, was a close friend and cousin of the Prophet. Ayeeshah was a prominent figure in early Islamic society and is remembered for her contributions to Islamic scholarship and her role as a mother to several of the Prophet's children.
